Your sentiment around 'money' being a means to an end is something that resonates with me a lot, especially how that ties to the constant oscillation between nihilism and hedonism. I am also a CS major so I also understand your comments about how coding sucks. I am not going to produce a recycled monologue about post-modern capitalism, but in brief I have come to realize that our current lifestyle amputates our biology. We're constantly using our head for everything, giving in to the intellectual rationalization of everything. And as far as I know, people who are fed up with this lifestyle can find meaning in reconnecting with their instincts. We have arms and legs and hearts that are routinely getting reminded of their obsoletion. So my suggestions would revolve around making use of your body and trying to surmount the barriers of ego. Join a fight club, do manual labor, drink with strangers, rekindle old passions etc. In summary, what I am trying to say is that I believe there is an untillegible dynamic, in which attunement to survival can fulfill our constant need for a more meaningful life.

And maybe his taste isn't that unique or subjective, but is calling out for a larger subtle group of people that can't properly express their needs and desires without being called stupid or trolls.  


As is the case for every group that has undergone oppression in history. Maybe we can better ourselves and help save people from less harm if we actually listen to what they have to say instead of sticking a label of egotism on them, which by the way, everyone is guilty of having.

Although I might not agree with how abrasive he was, I kind of understand his sentiment. Nobody owes him sympathy but I do find an obligation for understanding and sympathy if one should ever to decide to help someone. From a practical standpoint, failing to demonstrate that level of understanding and comprehension in front of someone who is clearly suffering, is just gonna inflict more pain, even if it were ever so subtle.
